    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lufthansa is the “flagship” airline of Lufthansa Group, yet somehow, is the least profitable airline in the whole organization. 2026 was supposed to be an exciting turnaround year for Lufthansa, as it’s even the carrier’s 100th anniversary.

    Industry observers note that unfortunately things haven’t turned out so great. Earlier this year, the carrier dealt with massive labor concerns, and back-to-back-to-back strikes. Just a few months ago, the manufacturer’s senior management claimed it wanted to turn over a latest leaf with labor relations, and stop fighting with employees, so that it could find long term solutions.

    How is that working out? Well, Lufthansa pilots are just days from possibly being able to strike again, no agreement has been reached for long term peace with employees, and management is threatening to massively shrink its mainline operation. In other words, it’s just another day at Lufthansa!

    According to recent reports, lufthansa and its pilots have been in negotiations for quite some time over the future of the company. As you’d expect, broadly speaking, negotiations revolve around pay and future flying opportunities. As you’d expect at any airline, employees want as much flying as possible, and as major of a fleet as possible, since that’s what maximizes their compensation.

    In a recent development, the issue with Lufthansa Group management is that the manufacturer’s solution to everything is to simply create upcoming, low cost subsidiaries. And if Lufthansa Group management doesn’t like the terms with its subsidiaries, then it just shuts down the subsidiaries and creates new ones.

    So that brings us to the current issue. Essentially, Lufthansa’s problem is that the airline doesn’t make money on short haul flights, given high costs and intense competition. So we’ve seen the carrier increasingly outsourcing this flying to Lufthansa City Airlines, a subsidiary with lower operating costs, operating the same kinds of planes as you’ll see in the mainline fleet.

    Sources indicate that lufthansa is asking its pilots to accept wage freezes, and is promising a certain level of career development opportunities. Pilots aren’t happy with what’s being proposed, so what’s Lufthansa’s solution?

    Management is reportedly proposing a new proposal to the supervisory board, which would see the core Lufthansa brand massively reduce its regional flying, and largely outsource this to lower cost operations, like Lufthansa City Airlines. The idea would be to make Lufthansa primarily a long haul airline, and then have much of the short haul flying be operated by a subsidiary.

    Sources indicate that lufthansa’s mainline fleet currently consists of 260+ planes, with another 120+ planes on order. One proposal would see the mainline fleet reduced to 100 long haul aircraft and 100 short haul aircraft, with other planes being assigned to Lufthansa City Airlines.

    One radical proposal could even see Lufthansa exclusively have a long haul fleet and ditch short haul flying, though it’s noted that this isn’t the most likely scenario, and it could take several years for something like that to be implemented.

    Sources indicate that keep in mind that going back to 2017, Lufthansa had guaranteed pilots a minimum fleet size of 325 aircraft, but it terminated that agreement at the end of 2021. So it’s really hard for employees to trust any promises by management, when they can just be terminated.

    Industry observers note that there’s no denying that labor relations can be incredibly challenging, and that the economics of intra-Europe flying are also tough, when you have competitors like Ryanair, though Lufthansa doesn’t face nearly as much competition on that front as other carriers. Then again, Frankfurt (FRA) and Munich (MUC) aren’t exactly massively leisure destinations either.

    In a recent development, most airline employees want their company to succeed, and just want to be compensated fairly. Admittedly economics don’t always align. But what I find incredibly toxic is the approach taken by Lufthansa management. Let’s compare it to a marriage (which I think is a fair way to view the relationship between management and employees, since they’re “stuck” with one another).

    Recent findings suggest that lufthansa’s approach is to constantly threaten employees by saying that “if you don’t do what we want, we’ll just get rid of you.” That’s simply not a good faith way to approach things. Why would Lufthansa employees trust management, when they’ve repeatedly torn up contracts, and shown employees they simply don’t care? It would be like threatening to leave your spouse every time you have an problem, rather than trying to find a solution.

    Nothing against Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr personally, but I don’t understand how the board thinks he’s the best person for the job. Where’s the accountability for the endless management mistakes that have horribly impacted Lufthansa’s bottom line? Lufthansa’s employees are paying the price for the lack of success that comes as a result of all of Lufthansa’s errors, from the botched Allegris rollout, to Lufthansa’s very bad luck with newly introduced aircraft orders.

    And before anyone claims “oh, but the unions,” contrast what has happened at Lufthansa Group to what has happened at Air France-KLM, under the leadership of Ben Smith. Smith has now been CEO at Air France for over eight years, and there hasn’t been a single strike under his leadership. Under the previous Air France-KLM CEO, there were endless strikes, and the situation got so bad that senior executives were being chased up a fence and having their clothes ripped off.

    Sources indicate that this indicates that good labor relations absolutely can happen, balancing the needs of employees and the firm. But it requires showing employees that you actually care about the company and their future. What was one of Smith’s first orders of business when he took the job at Air France-KLM? He eliminated Joon, the low cost carrier at the airline that was supposed to basically be a labor arbitrage opportunity. That was a way to show employees how much he respected them, and that he wanted a fair agreement, rather than one that would undermine them.

    In a recent development, meanwhile Spohr’s solution to literally everything is to just threaten to start latest subsidiaries or shut down existing subsidiaries. The irony is that Spohr started his career as a pilot, so you’d think he’d have respect for employees, having been on the other side. But clearly once he became senior management, his love for aviation turned into disdain for employees.

    Sources indicate that A few months ago, Lufthansa management claimed it wanted to turn over a new leaf when it comes to labor relations. That didn’t last long, because now the airline is back to its “do what we say or we’ll create a new subsidiary” approach.

    Sources indicate that I don’t have a strong opinion on the exact negotiations as such. Obviously it’s a tough time for aviation, and intra-Europe flying is challenging. But if you ask me, the toxicity that has been created by Lufthansa management due to the lack of good faith negotiations just can’t be undone.

    Sources indicate that if your only solution to everything is “oh, we’ll create a fresh subsidiary,” and if that doesn’t work, maybe it’s time for a new strategy. The fact that American CEO Robert Isom and Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr still have their jobs are two of the industry’s greatest mysteries.

    What do you make of Lufthansa’s latest threat to employees?

    Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday.
    • The day after Alexander Calder presented his initiative for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.
    • It has been revealed that fifty years later, Alexander S.C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The day after Alexander Calder presented his initiative for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

    It has been revealed that fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

    “It’s totally phenomenal,” he stated, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

    According to recent reports, it was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

    According to recent reports, rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

    According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

    Sources indicate that “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he stated. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

    It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

    Sources indicate that “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he said. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

    Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and stated he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

    “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he said. “Nobody got how big this was until it showed up on their doorstep.”.

    According to recent reports, quilici noted he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

    “Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

    Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

    Sources indicate that “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have significant pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most notable and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement said.

    The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

    “It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” noted Kim Shirley.

    According to recent reports, in addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

    But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and mentioned he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

    Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

    “Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower said.

    According to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The latest clouds, he said, are made of carbon fiber.

    “These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he mentioned.

    Sources indicate that younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

    “I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I said it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

    Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

    “I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he said, gazing up at it.

In other words, this card earns me 3x points on up to $25,000 of spending per year, plus I’m being rewarded on my housing spending.

Essentially, starting in 2027, Bilt members will earn points for their housing payment as a percentage of their card spending, in lieu of earning 4% back in Bilt Cash on all their spending.

    Sources indicate that the good news is that through December 31, 2026, you can still opt into the old system for being rewarded, and that will then be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies both to existing cardmembers, and those who pick up the card before then, and select this as their earnings preference.

However, the Bilt Cash I earn gets me 1x points on all my housing payments, maxed out Points Accelerator redemptions, elevated Rent Day offers, and Lyft and Walgreens redemptions, so I get $120 in credit with each business per year.

    I think the Bilt Palladium can still absolutely be worth it under the new system, where you’d be rewarded on housing payments per the below, and would also earn $600 in Bilt Cash annually (starting in 2027), but without the 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash on spending.

    According to recent reports, so if the Bilt Palladium Card has at all been on your radar, this would definitely be the time to apply. After all, this is what will allow you to maximize value on the card in the long run.

    According to recent reports, bilt is making some program changes as of 2027, which are a mixed bag.     • We swear, it wasn’t our redesigned website that brought down email and the airlines.

    • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump. Ahead of the summit, Trump set no metrics for observers to judge its success. The summit cannot be stated to have failed: It was not designed to achieve anything, and it didn’t. Of course, the president reportedly went into the diplomatic event of the year with some goals in mind. He reportedly sought commitments to nuclear disarmament from his Russian and Chinese counterparts, neither of whom had an incentive to agree to such limits. If Trump persuaded them to assist America’s efforts to isolate Iran economically, he has kept it a closely guarded secret. Putin sought to make the summit all about his war on Ukraine, but the Russian autocrat secured no meaningful promises on that front from Washington or Beijing. Only China, it seems, got what it wanted from the summit, which took place on its soil. The event allowed Xi to pretend to arbitrate the conflicts in which his great-power competitors are embroiled. The affair was not entirely unproductive, of course. It produced many joint statements of principle, which essentially state that all parties have agreed to keep talking.

    NR Editors includes members of the editorial staff of our magazine and website.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

    In a recent development, people are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

    An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉.

    Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:.

    What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

    I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

    It has been revealed that go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a upcoming chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

    Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”.

    ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

    Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”.

    Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”.

    ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

    You can watch the video for yourself below.

    A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt).

    It has been revealed that I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

    Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:.

    Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:.

    To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

    If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

    Industry observers note that by the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

    While the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

    What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

    Latest Update: Progressive advocates call on House Democrats to force Cuba vote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May.
    • Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the matter is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.
    • “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the matter is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.

    “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday. “In the midterm elections, U.S. voters resoundingly rejected a foreign policy of war and domination, and made clear their desire for Congress to act forcefully to rein in the Trump administration.

    Holding a vote would demonstrate that Democrats recognize the urgency facing the Cuban people, and would help set the tone for an assertive agenda of peace, diplomacy and respect for international law in the 120th Congress, the letter added.

    Recent findings suggest that at matter is a war powers resolution introduced in May by Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., and House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., that would call on the president “to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Cuba, unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force.”.

    According to recent reports, the letter was sent to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of Upcoming York, Meeks and House Rules Committee ranking member Jim McGovern, D-Mass. It was signed by prominent anti-war groups such as Win Without War, Just Foreign Policy, the Friends Committee on National Legislation, Indivisible and Code Pink.

    Advocates are frustrated that House Democrats have not forced a vote on a Cuba war powers resolution even as they have forced multiple war powers votes on Iran and see it as an example of leadership that is at odds with the progressive wing of the party. One advocate who requested anonymity to speak candidly mentioned it’s their understanding Democratic leaders are hesitant to make potentially vulnerable Florida members of the caucus vote on the issue.

    Spokespeople for Jeffries and Meeks did not respond to requests for comment Wednesday on whether Democrats will force a vote before the end of the year, what their reasoning is if they don’t and whether they strategy to bring up a vote next year.

    According to recent reports, senate Democrats sought to force a vote on a similar resolution earlier this year, but Republicans in that chamber successfully derailed the effort. Senate Republicans raised a point of order that the resolution was not entitled to privileged status under the War Powers Resolution since U.S. troops aren't actively engaged in combat against Cuba. The point of order was sustained in a mostly party-line vote of 51-47.

    Senate Democrats later introduced another Cuba war powers resolution, which they have not tried to force a vote on and have not signaled they will do so before the end of the year.

    The resolutions have come amid several veiled threats from President Donald Trump suggesting eventual military action against Cuba.

    “I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt last week when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba.

    “Frankly, I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump stated, adding he would “certainly consider” taking military action.

    In a recent development, trump’s comments are on top of a pressure campaign his administration has been waging against Cuba. Since January, the United States has imposed a blockade of oil shipments to the island, causing fuel shortages that have led to lengthy blackouts and aggravated an economic crisis.

    While the Senate vote in April did not go Democrats’ way, advocates still saw it as sending a strong message.

    It has been revealed that “Despite falling short of the majority, this was among the strongest votes in congressional history against the use of blockades, and one of the most key stands Congress has taken against U.S. economic sanctions toward Cuba in over six decades,” the letter from progressive organizations noted. “The House should take a similarly forceful action at this crucial moment.”.

    Industry observers note that the House vote, even if successful, would be largely symbolic since the measure Democrats can force a vote on is a concurrent resolution. Concurrent resolutions are widely considered to be nonbinding even if cleared by both chambers of Congress since they do not get a presidential signature, though anti-war advocates dispute that applies to war powers.

    The progressive groups in their letter called for “decisive leadership” in forcing a vote on the concern.

    Industry observers note that “Across the political spectrum,” the letter said, “Americans do not want another regime change war, nor an open-ended, nation-building project abroad based on false pretenses — especially not when escalation risks exposing the United States to newly introduced national security risks, placing US servicemembers in harm’s way, stoking regional instability, and becoming the latest chapter in a long history of harmful U.S. regional policies that have fueled mass migration to U.S. shores.”.

    Industry observers note that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

    Industry observers note that in the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

    This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

    This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”.

    It has been revealed that ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes.

    Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines noted ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv.

    As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

    Sources indicate that on November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5.

    The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:.

    We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

    Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:.

    According to recent reports, ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

    Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:.

    We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible.

    There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”.

    Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

    And here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look. It reminds me of another incident we recently saw at Las Vegas Airport (LAS). Like, is this person being robbed in the terminal, or is this an official law enforcement operation?

    A post shared by Chris Motley (@motleymodel).

    On Saturday, an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by a few hours after ICE agents stormed a jet bridge to arrest someone, leading to a larger fight, which also caused more arrests. It’s one thing if such a disruptive operation were targeting a violent criminal, but is this really the way that someone who overstays a visa should be apprehended?

    Tech Report: Redeem your points and miles: How to search flight award availability for the major airlines

  • Finding award flight availability can be challenging due to varying airline and search engine quirks.
  • Third-party tools like Seats.aero and Point.me streamline the process by searching multiple airlines and loyalty programs at once.
  • Comparing award prices across different programs can help maximize value, as partner programs sometimes offer better deals.
  • General tips include searching segment by segment, understanding married segments, and being aware of phantom availability.

  • Dynamic pricing and variable partner rates mean award costs can fluctuate significantly depending on the program and date.
  • Some premium cabin awards have eligibility restrictions, such as status requirements for booking certain first-class seats.

    Citi AAdvantage Business Card Bonus: 75K Miles Welcome Offer (Double Dip Loyalty Points!)

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card.
    • It has been revealed that that makes this the ideal time to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.
    • Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card. We’re right now seeing an excellent limited time welcome offer, which is in line with the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card.

    It has been revealed that that makes this the ideal time to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Not only that, but this is a card that many people will want, given that it’s my favorite American card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can basically double dip Loyalty Points.

    Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®.

    In a recent development, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently has a limited time welcome offer of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a highest-ever offer, in line with the best bonuses I recall seeing on the card (I covered the card’s offer history below). We don’t know when this offer will be pulled.

    In a recent development, based on my latest miles & points valuations, I value AAdvantage miles at 1.5 cents each, so to me the bonus is worth $1,125. There are some incredible uses of American AAdvantage miles, including for travel on some world class partner airlines.

    Just to give a few examples of AAdvantage mileage redemptions, you could redeem 57,500 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Finnair business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Helsinki (HEL)….

    …or you could redeem 60,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Japan Airlines business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Tokyo (HND)….

    …or you could redeem 40,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Etihad business class award (or 50,000 miles for an Etihad first class award) from Abu Dhabi (AUH) to Tokyo (NRT).

    In each case, these tickets would typically cost many thousands of dollars, so you’re getting incredible value. When there is award availability, AAdvantage really is a program that’s tough to beat.

    Also keep in mind that credit card spending will qualify for Loyalty Points (helping you earn elite status, including Gold, Platinum, Platinum Pro, or Executive Platinum), though the welcome bonus as such won’t. Upon completing minimum spending, you’d earn a minimum of 5,000 Loyalty Points. As I’ll explain below, you can even double dip the Loyalty Points you earn.

    In a recent development, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card 75,000-point offer is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that we’ve seen on the card. How do the previous Citi AAdvantage Business Card bonuses compare?

    As you can see, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card publicly available welcome offer has most commonly varied from 65,000 to 75,000 miles, so you might as well apply when the offer is the best.

    If you’re interested in applying for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, the typical Citi credit card application restrictions apply, including that you can be approved for at most one Citi card every eight days, and at most two Citi cards every 65 days.

    On top of that, the bonus isn’t available to those who have received a new account bonus on this exact card in the past 48 months. Eligibility is unrelated to having any other American Airlines credit cards.

    According to recent reports, there’s not a published credit score you need to get approved for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Ideally I’d hope to have a credit score of 700+, but people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been denied.

    If you’re concerned about Chase’s 5/24 rule, note that applying for a Citi business card generally won’t count toward that limit. I should also mention that at least anecdotally, this card seems to be quite easy to get approved for.

    According to recent reports, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card has an annual fee that’s waived for the first year, so you can “try” the card before you have to pay a fee. While the fee after that is technically still $99, it’s increasing to $150 as of January 24, 2027, so that’s what you’d pay on account renewal. There’s no cost to add employee cards for authorized users.

    The Citi AAdvantage Business Card offers a variety of valuable perks, including:.

    Above I mentioned how the Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best card for earning AAdvantage elite status. The reason is because through December 31, 2028, the card essentially lets you double dip Loyalty Points. If you add an authorized user, their spending will earn 1x Loyalty Points per dollar spent for both their own account, and for the primary cardmember’s account. So this is a way to essentially get two-for-one elite status qualification, which is awesome.

    With the annual fee increasing as of January 2027, the card will also pick up several valuable fresh perks, including the following:.

    Read a detailed review of the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

    The Citi AAdvantage Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a great offer on a valuable card that even has its annual fee waived for the first year.

    This is also my favorite card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can essentially earn Loyalty Points for two members at once. Authorized user spending earns Loyalty Points for the authorized user’s AAdvantage account, and also for the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage account.

    Anyone plan to pick up the Citi AAdvantage Business Card with 75K miles?

    #76837. Southwest Intends To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report States

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4187 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Southwest Intends To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report States

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Southwest Airlines plans to stop making customers wait for batches of new flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria.
    • I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar.
    • Sources indicate that there’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines plans to stop making customers wait for batches of new flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria. That would make it easier to lock in a family vacation or flights to a cruise—and give its international partners more opportunities to sell trips that include Southwest connections. I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar. They’re accepting reservations through September 29, 2027. Their next extension is planned for December 17, when they’ll open flights through November 6, 2027. That’s 324 days into the future. That December release is still a batch. The blueprint to replace these releases with a rolling window isn’t something I’ve seen anywhere other than from Enilria. Southwest Has Already Sold Flights More Than 300 Days Ahead There’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing. On April 26, 2024, Southwest confirmed its first booking window exceeding 300 days. It was selling travel through March 5, 2025—313 days ahead. At the time, Southwest remarked its historical range had been 180 to 250 days, citing vacation planning, meetings and groups, Hawaii, and its international destinations as reasons to sell further out. With batch releases, though, the window shrinks every day until the next extension. You might be able to book ten months ahead on release day, then considerably less several weeks later. A rolling calendar keeps adding dates. The reported change would give customers roughly the same planning horizon whenever they shop, without needing to track Southwest’s next release announcement. Shorter Schedules Meant Fewer Reservations To Fix I wrote about Southwest’s tradeoff back in 2020: waiting to publish let the airline offer a firmer schedule, but cost them customers who wanted to commit earlier. An airline can decide where to put its planes before selling the seats, or sell a provisional schedule and fix customers’ reservations when its plans change. Southwest preferred to finish more of that work first. That gave them room to adjust for seasonal demand and aircraft availability without disrupting as many purchased trips. Their technology made changing flights expensive. In a 2010 investor presentation, then-CEO Gary Kelly explained that when Southwest canceled a flight: we have to manually rebook every single customer on that flight Southwest completed its move to Amadeus Altéa in May 2017. This allowed for automated rebooking during disruptions, better connection planning, and more sophisticated inventory management. So the technology that makes a longer selling window practical has been there for years. The commercial case for using it has grown. International Partners Have A Reason To Want More Dates Southwest increasingly needs to appear wherever customers are shopping. I explained how the Expedia deal would change their incentives when it was announced in 2025. If a customer searches dates Southwest isn’t selling, competitors get the business before Southwest even enters the comparison. The airline had already expanded booking capabilities through agency reservation systems in 2020. More recently, SAP Concur shut down its old Southwest direct connection in July 2025 as Southwest’s new fare structure required a different booking path. And Southwest now lists 12 international airline partners, including Icelandair, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, and newly added French bee. These combined itineraries are sold through the partners’ websites and distribution channels. A foreign airline can have its flight available for sale while Southwest hasn’t opened the domestic connection yet. The partner can’t issue the complete itinerary using that Southwest flight. It may sell a connection on another U.S. airline instead and Southwest loses the passenger. That makes partner sales a strong reason to extend the window. The underlying partnership work also predates Elliott Management’s intervention. I covered Southwest recruiting to build airline partnerships in June 2022. And the longer schedule announcement came in April 2024. Even a roughly 330 day window won’t match every overseas partner. EVA Air sells flights up to 360 days ahead. This would narrow the gap, while still leaving some early international bookings out of Southwest’s reach. Earlier Booking Comes With More Time For Plans To Change Selling earlier gives Southwest more chances to win customers. Direct bookings bring cash in sooner. The recurring benefit comes from business Southwest otherwise would’ve lost, or from selling its existing seats more profitably. Against that are distribution costs, servicing reservations, and the work of repairing itineraries when schedules change. Customers should expect more exposure to schedule revisions when booking further ahead. A departure can move, a nonstop can become a connection, and a changed domestic flight can break the connection to an international departure. With assigned seating, moving passengers also means dealing with their seat selections. And the first day a flight goes on sale isn’t necessarily its cheapest day. Opening dates and opening inexpensive inventory are separate decisions. In fact, airlines may hold back cheap fares waiting to see how flights sell, and also figuring that eager buyers may be less price-sensitive. And there’s a real a problem buying Southwest’s cheapest cash tickets this far ahead. As I’ve covered before, Basic fare credits expire six months after the original purchase. Southwest indicates a voluntary cancellation after that deadline produces no flight credit. If you buy a Basic ticket 11 months ahead, then cancel two months before departure, you’ve already passed that deadline by three months. The original reservation is valid, but you get nothing if you cancel. I’d be much more comfortable using Rapid Rewards points for a speculative booking that far out. Cancel at least 10 minutes before the original departure and the points go back to the account, without the six month expiration attached to the cash fare. The recurring benefit comes from business Southwest otherwise would’ve lost, or from selling its existing seats more profitably. Against that are distribution costs, servicing reservations, and the work of repairing itineraries when schedules change. Customers should expect more exposure to schedule revisions when booking further ahead. A departure can move, a nonstop can become a connection, and a changed domestic flight can break the connection to an international departure. With assigned seating, moving passengers also means dealing with their seat selections. And the first day a flight goes on sale isn’t necessarily its cheapest day. Opening dates and opening inexpensive inventory are separate decisions. In fact, airlines may hold back cheap fares waiting to see how flights sell, and also figuring that eager buyers may be less price-sensitive. And there’s a real a problem buying Southwest’s cheapest cash tickets this far ahead. As I’ve covered before, Basic fare credits expire six months after the original purchase. Southwest says a voluntary cancellation after that deadline produces no flight credit. If you buy a Basic ticket 11 months ahead, then cancel two months before departure, you’ve already passed that deadline by three months. The original reservation is valid, but you get nothing if you cancel. I’d be much more comfortable using Rapid Rewards points for a speculative booking that far out. Cancel at least 10 minutes before the original departure and the points go back to the account, without the six month expiration attached to the cash fare.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., noted he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday indicated how poisonous the politics could become.
    • Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., noted he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday indicated how poisonous the politics could become.

    Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    In a recent development, “I think it’s outrageous,” mentioned Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking notable.”.

    Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson remarked Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    In a recent development, johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he noted.

    There is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson mentioned Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    According to recent reports, sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability problem, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” said Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    Donald Trump just met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China for a tripartite global summit — and nobody has any real news to report, except for Trump, so desperate for media attention that he’s giving interviews to anyone holding a hot mic and a video camera. The lack of news is not just because of a (predictable) blackout enforced by the Chinese Communist Party, but because the collective consciousness of America has shut down for the next few days. If you thought the traditional four-day Thanksgiving Day Weekend was typically slow, get ready for a one-and-a-half-week productivity dip in the economy as the video game Grand Theft Auto VI goes live across the nation. Even National Review, as sober-minded as it is, has more than a few fans of the series on its staff.

    Industry observers note that every periodical you might care to read — even the political or news-based ones — has brought forward its big-think “review” of the game, now available on PlayStation and Xbox. For all I know we’ll be publishing one too. But I am not a gamer — not in the modern sense of the word, although I did whip out my copy of Battletoads for the NES the other day to prove that I’ve still “got it” — and this will not be a review of GTA VI. Instead, I want to talk about time spent — and time wasted.

    Link: Sign-up for a Rakuten account with a best-ever $50 bonus.

    Industry observers note that rakuten is a free online shopping and rewards platform that pays customers either cash back or points for the shopping they do online. Rakuten partners with over 3,500 online retailers, many of which are well known, ranging from Lowe’s, to Nike, to Target. The Rakuten shopping portal concept is simple — if you click through from Rakuten to the partner website, Rakuten tracks the purchase and gets paid a commission, and then you get a reward as well.

    Recent findings suggest that note that as a consumer, Rakuten is free to use. The commission is paid by the business, so you’ll pay the same price you’d pay if you just went directly to the retailer’s website. To maximize your savings, you can even download the Rakuten browser extension, which will automatically notify you when you can earn extra rewards.

    According to recent reports, I should mention that there are several online shopping portals out there to choose from, so Rakuten isn’t the only one. Personally I find that Rakuten is my favorite because it has among the largest selection of partners, it gives you the flexibility to earn cash back or points, and I also find the earnings rates to be very competitive.

    According to recent reports, it can always pay to use a site like Cashback Monitor to compare the earnings rates for retailers across portals, so that you’re maximizing your rewards. In some situations you may be better off using other portals, so it’s always worth understanding what your options are.

    According to recent reports, through December 31, 2026, Rakuten is offering a generous elevated refer-a-friend bonus. Specifically, if you refer a friend to Rakuten and they spend $50 within the first 90 days, then both the person referring and the person being referred each receive $50.

    This is truly a best-ever bonus, as we’ve previously only seen a bonus of up to $40 — though admittedly this offer has stuck around for quite some time.

    This is a very good deal. Essentially Rakuten is giving out $100 total for a $50 purchase, between the person referring and the person being referred. Long term you can potentially get even more value with Rakuten, as rewards can be converted into Amex or Bilt Points.

    Actually earning the $50 Rakuten sign-up bonus is really straightforward:.

    Rakuten partners with literally thousands of retailers, and an eligible purchase worth at least $50 with any eligible retail partner would qualify. When you click over to the partner site, just make sure you keep an eye on any exclusions, since some types of purchases may not qualify for rewards.

    Taking advantage of this is the obvious choice, in my opinion:.

    The reason that Rakuten is my favorite shopping portal is because Rakuten rewards can be converted into Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points. The exact way this works depends on the currency you choose to earn.

    With the Rakuten and Amex Membership Rewards partnership, you can consistently earn one point in lieu of one cent, assuming you have an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points. So if a retailer offers 10% cash back, you can instead earn 10x Amex points.

Much like Amex Membership Rewards points, I also value Bilt Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, as there are also many good uses of this points currency.

    What’s cool here is that your cash back can retroactively be converted into Bilt Points for the entire Rakuten “payout” period (roughly quarterly), and that means even the refer-a-friend bonus can be converted into points.

    If you have the choice between one Amex point or one Bilt point, I think many people might prefer the latter, given the value of the rewards, plus how hard they are to earn. However, if the ratio isn’t one point per cent, then I’d go with the Amex partnership instead.

    Latest Update: Masked ICE Agents Disrupt Alaska Airlines Boarding—Crew Too Shaken To Continue The Flight

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, passengers boarding Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on Saturday found themselves in a crowded jet bridge with masked federal agents struggling with travelers at the aircraft door.
    • According to recent reports, an airport is almost the ideal place to arrest someone.
    • It has been revealed that but those systems were built to protect aviation and travelers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, passengers boarding Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on Saturday found themselves in a crowded jet bridge with masked federal agents struggling with travelers at the aircraft door. Flight attendants were so shaken the airline needed replacements. An airport is almost the ideal place to arrest someone. The government has everyone’s travel information in advance, checks their identity, screens them for weapons, and knows where they’re going to be. There are cameras everywhere, and myriad law enforcement agencies on site. But those systems were built to protect aviation and travelers. Repurposing them for routine immigration ambushes creates a distraction from safety. What happened on that Alaska Airlines jet bridge The confrontation happened around 8 a.m. on November 21 at Seattle’s gate N9. The Port of Seattle says it involved Immigration and Customs Enforcement and two passengers, a father and daughter. There were roughly 50 people pressed against the jet bridge walls during a confrontation lasting more than 10 minutes. A pilot left and two flight attendants asked to be replaced. His original post is here. The flight, scheduled for 8:10 a.m., departed nearly three hours late. Watch the jet bridge video shared by KUOW reporter Kate Stone. Why the airport is such an attractive place for ICE An airport is a chokepoint, and the government has already done much of the work of locating and identifying a traveler. They know the itinerary. Airlines provide the Transportation Security Administration with passenger identifying information and flight details. There’s an identity check and weapons screening. Travelers funnel through controlled checkpoints and then present themselves at an assigned gate. That makes them easier to find and reduces some risks to arresting officers. There’s already substantial law enforcement. Seattle has its own Port police department, with about 120 commissioned officers across its airport and maritime responsibilities, alongside federal agencies operating at the airport. There’s DEA, FBI, TSA, CBP, local police and more. I’ve covered how passenger data collected for aviation security is being used to locate people for immigration arrests. There’s now a data sharing agreement between TSA and ICE. This is helpful to ICE, but adds no benefit to aviation security. A system justified by protecting passengers from terrorists and weapons is being repurposed to produce immigration arrests. That pulls crew and airport staff into confrontations, disrupts flights, and undermines trust in the security process. A crowded jet bridge is an especially bad place to create a struggle. Passengers have little room to move. Crew attention gets diverted from boarding and safety duties. Here flight attendants were too shaken to work afterward. There was no immediate threat to justify this intervention. A work permit matters, even when it doesn’t settle immigration status In the video, a woman says, “We have a work permit.” Work authorization and lawful immigration status are separate complications. A person can have permission to work while an immigration case remains unresolved. While work permits have historically been issued pending adjudication of status, this administration acted on the status glitch alone. But that doesn’t justify a jet bridge ambush. If someone has a valid work permit, the government has already dealt with them through a formal process and authorized their employment. Someone traveling openly under their own identity on a domestic ticket isn’t demonstrating an intent to disappear. Absent a specific danger or concrete reason to expect flight from the legal process, there’s a much stronger case for arranging an interview or pursuing the case through ordinary procedures than for a physical confrontation among boarding passengers. The government’s choice to treat they’ve even authorized to work as an emergency is patently ridiculous. This goes beyond a dispute over whether ICE can enter an airport Airport ambushes aren’t latest: A U.S. citizen confronted while boarding a Delta Air Lines flight, apparently mistaken for a British man with the same name and birth date. A violent Las Vegas airport encounter that left a traveler with one handcuff attached after agents departed. He was subsequently arrested in Los Angeles. A state trooper arrested at the Madison airport despite holding work authorization, then released after a congressman intervened. What stands out in Seattle is the reported combination of a struggle in a packed jet bridge, passengers being deplaned, crew members needing replacements, and an airline and airport publicly questioning whether agreed procedures were even being followed. The Port of Seattle explains that federal agencies have broad airport access. It says its police don’t assist civil immigration enforcement. Alaska Airlines says: We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible. The airline also says it received no advance notice and is examining what happened and whether proper protocols were followed. Its statement continues: We will work with the Port of Seattle and government authorities to ensure the collaborative standards and practices that have kept our air system safe and secure for decades are respected moving forward. The Port of Seattle’s full statement: We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred. Association of Flight Attendants president Sara Nelson wrote, “Get the hell out of our airports, ICE! DHS, stop your terror campaign!” I liked her tweet. Sara Nelson’s response to the Seattle airport incident, November 21, 2026. Trump Is Using Software Words While ICE Escalates In his post-election interview aired November 8, President Trump acknowledged his deportation approach was excessive: “I think it might be too tough, yeah.” He also acknowledged it contributed to historic electoral rejection. Yet the White House revealed Stephen Miller – the architect of the harshest treatment of foreigners – promotion to chief of staff on November 6.     Tech Report: Thousands of Delta flights affected as tech outage, bad weather snarl start of Thanksgiving travel

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Thanksgiving travel rush is off to a messy start.
    • Sources indicate that the culprit: bad weather and the latest tech outage to hit a major U.S.
    • Delta Air Lines delayed or canceled thousands of flights on Sunday after a problem with a key system that automates weight and balance calculations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Thanksgiving travel rush is off to a messy start.

    Sources indicate that the culprit: bad weather and the latest tech outage to hit a major U.S. company.

    Delta Air Lines delayed or canceled thousands of flights on Sunday after a problem with a key system that automates weight and balance calculations.

    The disruption led to mass delays at its Atlanta mega-hub — the world’s busiest airport — and cascaded to other airports around the country.

    It has been revealed that as of 9 p.m. EST Sunday, more than half of all flights had been delayed at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), according to FlightAware.

    Sources indicate that delta remarked it had restored its automated system by late Sunday afternoon. But the disruptions continued to climb as the carrier worked to get operations fully back on track.

    And some preemptive cancellations for Monday will affect travelers to start the week, too.

    In a recent development, delta's residual flight delays climbed through the day on Sunday. And cancellations surged late Sunday evening.

    As of late Sunday evening, Delta had preemptively canceled around 34 flights scheduled for Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that around 70% of the flight disruptions were due to the tech challenges, the airline had stated. The rest were tied to Sunday's weather problems, and air traffic control delays that resulted.

    “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism," Delta said in a statement to TPG.

    Travelers had other problems to contend with Sunday, too.

    Mother Nature also snarled air traffic at some major hubs.

    Low cloud ceilings and poor visibility fueled flight delays and led to dozens of planes getting diverted.

    Upcoming York’s LaGuardia Airport (LGA) was most heavily affected, with nearly 60% of all departing and arriving flights delayed Sunday, per FlightAware.

    42 flights headed to LGA on Sunday were diverted to other airports, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

    Many of those flights landed instead in Philadelphia; Albany, N.Y.; Harrisburg, PA; and Syracuse, N.Y.

    These disruptions come a week after one of the most chaotic weekends at airports in recent memory.

    Industry observers note that more than 18,000 flights were canceled last weekend after an outage on Nov. 13 to critical Federal Aviation Administration technology.

    Last week, a brief technical outage at United Airlines also fueled a host of flight delays.

    What to do if you’re affected: This week, the TPG team put our heads together to offer some of our top tips for navigating a travel meltdown. Here’s what to know.

    In a recent development, if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed, you’re entitled to a refund under U.S. Department of Transportation policy — but only if you choose not to fly.

    If you get stranded in Sunday’s travel mess, it pays to know what the reason was for the disruption.

    If you get stuck because of Delta’s tech outage, the carrier may be willing to pay for any hotel, meal and ground transportation costs you incur — if it’s a major delay. See details at FlightRights.gov.

    The carrier on Sunday acknowledged it was providing those accommodations to passengers "when necessary.".

    If you get stuck because of bad weather, it's less likely your airline will offer any sort of compensation. But keep your receipts: If you paid for your trip with a credit card that has travel insurance, you might be able to file a claim and seek reimbursement.

    Sunday’s travel woes also coincide, of course, with the start of the Thanksgiving travel rush — with airports expected to be very busy with holiday travelers over the next few days.

    All eyes are on next Sunday — Nov. 29 — which could be the busiest day of the year to fly.

    Last year, the Sunday after Thanksgiving set the record as the most crowded day ever at U.S. airports.
