    Alaska Atmos Rewards Business Card Review: 90K Points & Strong Perks

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
    • According to recent reports, the card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency.
    • Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. The card is issued by Bank of America, and is a rebranding of the former Alaska Airlines Visa Business Card.

    According to recent reports, the card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency. This post is my in-depth Atmos Rewards Business Card review, so I’d like to take a look at the card’s value proposition, for anyone who may be considering applying.

    Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    Before I get into my Atmos Rewards Business Card review, here’s a brief summary of the key details of the card:.

    Below are what I consider to be the pros and cons of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem. To start, let’s cover the welcome bonus, card eligibility rules, annual fee, and more, since these are key factors that cardmembers consider.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. This is the best publicly available bonus that we’ve ever seen on the card, and you can find the bonus offer history in this post.

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, Atmos Rewards points are worth 1.5 cents each, given the great uses of these rewards. That means the 90,000 points are worth $1,350 for me.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is issued by Bank of America. The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Plan cards.

    In a recent development, beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    Industry observers note that there’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    I should also mention the following restriction in the terms:.

    I also understand that I may be declined for additional credit card accounts if my business entity at the moment has, or has had, another business card with Bank of America in the preceding 24 month period.

    In a recent development, on the surface, this suggests you may be declined for a Bank of America business card if you have another Bank of America business card. However, anecdotally, this doesn’t appear to be enforced much. I think the term “may” is the key here (which is different than “will”).

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card has a $195 annual fee. That’s on the steep side, though the card does have some premium perks. The good news is that you can add employee cards at no extra cost, so that annual fee covers the cost for all the cards you’ll have.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 10x points per dollar spent on flights booked through the Atmos for Business website. If you’re looking to maximize your earning, this is where you want to book your Alaska and Hawaiian flights, as this is an incredible deal.

    You do need your own business to participate in the Atmos for Business program, and once registered, the return on spending is really tough to beat. Based on my valuation of points, that’s like an incremental 15% return on eligible airfare spending, on top of what you otherwise earn.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 3x points on all other eligible Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, with no caps. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 4.5% return on spending. So if you fly either of those Alaska Air Group carriers with any frequency, that’s a solid return on that spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 2x points on eligible dining purchases. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. It’s always nice to earn bonus points, though in fairness, 2x points isn’t exactly the biggest return on spending that we’ve seen.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 1x points on all other eligible spending. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. As you might expect, there are more exciting cards for everyday spending, as independently, that’s not a terribly exciting return.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card can help you earn elite status in the Atmos Rewards program. Specifically, the card offers one status point for every $3 in eligible spending. There’s no cap on how many status points you can earn with the card.

    If you are serious about earning status with spending, I’d recommend instead considering the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more), which offers one status point for every $2 in eligible spending.

    Beyond the ability to earn one status point per $3 spent, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers some additional threshold bonuses for spending, including bonus status points and discount codes:.

    It has been revealed that in other words, spending $200,000 per anniversary year would earn you 20,000 bonus status points, plus a discount code for 50% off a base fare. Just to cover the basics of that 50% off base fare discount code, here’s how that works:.

    So the value of this will depend on how you’d usually travel, but this could easily save you many hundreds of dollars, depending on the type of ticket you book. It’s also still possible to upgrade these tickets, but at least the initial booking has to be in economy.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card also offers a Bank of America relationship bonus. If you have an eligible small business Bank of America checking or savings account, you’ll receive a bonus equal to 10% of the points you earn on each dollar spent.

    This is a way to earn even more rewards, as you’d earn 11x points on Atmos for Business purchases, 3.3x points on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, 2.2x points on the other purchases eligible for bonus categories, and 1.1x points on everyday spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a decent card to use for purchases abroad, since you can rack up rewards without paying a fee.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a variety of benefits and credits, which can potentially more than justify the annual fee year after year. These perks are the main reason you want to consider picking up this card, in addition to the great welcome bonus. In no particular order, let’s go over the main benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a free checked bag for you and up to six guests on the same reservation when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized users on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card, so that’s a huge incentive to add authorized users to the card.

    This is a great benefit that could save you a lot of money — Alaska and Hawaiian ordinarily charge $30-45 per checked bag, so that’s a savings of up to $90 per person roundtrip, if checking bags. If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian fairly often but don’t have elite status, that alone could rapidly more than justify the annual fee.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers preferred boarding for you and up to six guests on the same reservation. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized customers on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card.

    This is a valuable benefit that helps you ensure that there’s space in the overhead bin for your bags. It’s also an awesome authorized user perk, so that you can share this benefit with others.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers four Alaska Lounge passes annually. The way this works, the primary cardmember will have one Alaska Lounge pass deposited into their Atmos Rewards account at the beginning of the quarter, valid through the end of the quarter.

    Industry observers note that each is valid for access to Alaska Lounges on a single calendar day, in conjunction with a same day flight operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, a oneworld airline, or an Alaska global partner. Each pass is valid for one adult, plus accompanying children. For what it’s worth, a day pass would otherwise cost $60 per person.

    It has been revealed that if you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you can share your Atmos Rewards points with other members at no cost. The way this works, you can link your accounts with up to 10 other Atmos Rewards members (they don’t have to be family — accounts of friends are fine as well), and then you can move points back and forth for free.

    I’d argue that this is especially compelling for families, because it’s easier to rack up a sizable balance of points when you can consolidate them into one account.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 20% back on Alaska and Hawaiian inflight purchases when paying with your card. This applies for the purchase of food, beverages, and Wi-Fi onboard flights, and the statement credit should post to your account within seven days. There’s no limit to how often you can take advantage of this.

    Let me just mention that Alaska and Hawaiian should have free Starlink Wi-Fi fleetwide by some point in 2027, at which point there won’t be savings anymore with Wi-Fi. That being mentioned, it can still be used for food and beverages.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, then you’re eligible for a free same day confirmed flight change on Alaska. This ordinarily costs $50 per person, so that’s quite valuable.

    With this, you can change to another flight that might be more convenient, subject to capacity controls. This is especially useful in high frequency markets.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’re eligible to receive a $50 voucher if you have an Alaska flight that is delayed by at least two hours, or that’s canceled within 24 hours of departure.

    The $50 voucher is valid for 48 hours, and will be delivered to the email address associated with the reservation, and can be used for food, drinks, etc. Travel must have been booked directly with Alaska using the eligible credit card.

    Those with the Atmos Rewards Business Card receive up to a $120 airport security credit every four years, in connection with TSA PreCheck or Global Entry. This is a perk offered by many premium credit cards, and there’s lots of value to this.

    It has been revealed that when talking about an Atmos Rewards credit card, it’s worth acknowledging the general value in earning and redeeming Atmos Rewards points. Alaska & Hawaiian are both in the oneworld alliance, and Atmos Rewards partners not only with oneworld partner airlines, but also with all kinds of other unaligned airlines. I consider Atmos Rewards to be one of the most valuable points currencies out there.

    In a recent development, atmos Rewards has a distance based award chart, which varies a bit by region. For example, below is the one-way award chart within the Americas.

    It has been revealed that I constantly redeem Atmos Rewards points for travel within the United States, particularly on American. For example, all the time I redeem 4,500 points to fly one-way economy from Miami to Tampa (when cash fares would often be $200+), or 15,000 points to fly one-way business class from Miami to Chicago or New York (when cash fares would often be $500+). You simply can’t beat these redemption rates.

    The icing on the cake is that with Atmos Rewards, you earn status points for award flights, so those flights even count toward elite status, and that’s also why I’ve switched my business to Atmos Rewards.

    Of course there are lots of other opportunities with Atmos Rewards points as well. For example, I love the ability to redeem 75,000 points for one-way business class from the United States to many parts of Asia on carriers like Japan Airlines or Starlux Airlines — those are both awards that I’ve booked for myself in the past, and they were a great value.

    Industry observers note that what makes this an even better value is that you can have a free stopover on a one-way award when traveling long haul. One thing worth being aware of is that Atmos Rewards has a $20 per person per direction partner award booking fee. However, that can be waived if you have the Atmos Rewards Summit Card.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, so how valuable is this product? A few thoughts….

    According to recent reports, first of all, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking up this card for the excellent welcome bonus, which includes a lot of points. The card also has significant ongoing benefits. The card also doesn’t count toward the Chase 5/24 limit, which is nice. Given the value of the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, there’s no reason not to pick up this card, if eligible.

    According to recent reports, what about the long term value proposition of the card, though? If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency and don’t have elite status, the basic perks add up, including a first checked bag free, preferred boarding, a quarterly lounge pass, free points sharing, and more.

    However, I’d say there’s also merit to picking up one (or both) of the personal Atmos Rewards cards….

    The $395 annual fee Atmos Rewards Summit Card is the most premium Atmos Rewards credit card. While it’s a personal card, I still think it’s worth highlighting, as it’s incredibly lucrative. I’d take it a step further, and say that it’s my favorite airline credit card.

    Among other things, the card racks up status points at the fastest rate, the card allows you to earn Global Companion Awards, offers Alaska Lounge passes, enables free points sharing, waives partner award booking fees, offers 3x points on foreign purchases, and much more.

    If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency, then getting this card is an absolute no-brainer. As I see it, the anniversary 25K-point Global Companion Award alone basically justifies the annual fee, and that indicates nothing of all the other amazing perks.

    If you’re not set on an Atmos Rewards Business Card but want a dedicated business credit card that’s lucrative, there are some other great options that earn flexible points. Consider these if you want options for redeeming your rewards for more than just on Alaska, Hawaiian, and its partners:.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is an excellent business credit card that offers a massive welcome bonus and strong perks. The limited time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points will come in handy for cardmembers, and is more than enough reason to get the card.

    In a recent development, if you don’t yet have this card and are eligible, I’d highly recommend applying. This is a card that many people don’t have, yet which offers lots of value and a great bonus.

    If you want to learn more about or apply for the Atmos Rewards Business Card, follow this link.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A Frontier Airlines passenger notes she refused to get off her San Francisco–Denver flight until a flight attendant apologized to her four year old son.
    • I don’t think asking for a little help with a frightened child is outrageous.
    • In a recent development, she indicates her son was afraid of loud toilet flushes and needed the bathroom about 40 minutes before landing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A Frontier Airlines passenger notes she refused to get off her San Francisco–Denver flight until a flight attendant apologized to her four year old son. The argument began with a request to flush the toilet after the frightened boy had left the lavatory. The mother says things escalated when she overheard the crew member making fun of his fear. I don’t think asking for a little help with a frightened child is outrageous. If the flight attendant mocked him, an apology was appropriate. But the mother wasn’t entitled to make getting off the aircraft conditional on receiving one. She says her son was afraid of loud toilet flushes and needed the bathroom about 40 minutes before landing. She tried offering headphones and offering to flush for him. Eventually she reassured him that they could ask a flight attendant to help. She says she asked the flight attendant near the lavatory to flush after they’d washed their hands and left. The response was, He can flush it. It’s not that loud. The flight attendant added that this was a fresh plane. The mother says she dropped the request, but while she and her son were inside the lavatory, she heard the crew member talking to a colleague: Can you believe that mom? Scared of a toilet? Come on. She says her son heard it too and asked whether they were talking about him. The mother flushed the toilet herself, with her son waiting outside and the door closed. At deplaning she confronted the flight attendant and demanded an apology to the boy. She says the crewmember responded “Have a good day,” so she confirmed: I’m not getting off this airplane until you apologize to my son for literally making fun of him for being afraid of something. A pilot emerged from the cockpit, the flight attendant apologized, and she left. She also says a couple of passengers applauded and another mother praised her. She’s since posted a clarification: she says she also asked the flight attendant to stand with her son while she flushed. She also says her analytics show viewers watched an average of 23% of the original video and that’s why so many people seem to have missed that she did, in fact, flush the toilet herself. She wanted help pressing a button once they were away, or standing beside the child briefly. A polite refusal would be reasonable. In terms of what the flight attendant’s actual duty is, the union contract‘s article 23.I assigns general tidying and replenishing lavatory supplies, but says, “Flight Attendants will not clean the aircraft.” Pushing the button isn’t cleaning, but they don’t have broad lavatory duties. The claim that it’s a new airplane doesn’t mean the toilet isn’t loud. Aircraft vacuum toilets can be startling. Brigham Young University researchers spent two years developing a quieter aircraft toilet, citing parents’ concerns about children being afraid to use them. A quieter cabin can even make the flush stand out more. I’ve written about flight attendants mocking passengers for using the bathroom during boarding. The mother makes herself much harder to sympathize with in her video, though. She calls the employee an “old bitch” and tells her to “know your f’ing role.” I sided with the expectation that parents clean up after their children when Anthony Bass complained about his pregnant wife being asked to pick up their child’s popcorn on United. Parents should take responsibility. And her refusal to leave is absurd. Complain to the airline, don’t inconvenience other passengers trying to get off the plane.     Delta Pilot Reportedly Fired For Answering His Phone While Taxiing—Similar Stories Go Back At Least 5 Years

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A Delta Air Lines first officer allegedly answered his cellphone while taxiing out in Atlanta on his first trip at the airline.
    • The first officer was reportedly flying trips under a check pilot’s supervision as part of their initial operating experience.
    • The Black Box Aviation Podcast’s account, November 17, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A Delta Air Lines first officer allegedly answered his cellphone while taxiing out in Atlanta on his first trip at the airline. The captain returned to the gate, had him removed, and the new hire lost his job, according to an account shared by the Black Box Aviation Podcast and covered by Live and Let’s Fly. The first officer was reportedly flying trips under a check pilot’s supervision as part of their initial operating experience. The Black Box Aviation Podcast’s account, November 17, 2026 There’s no identified pilot, flight number, aircraft type or date for the alleged incident. The podcast’s companion article repeats the allegation but doesn’t fill in those details. A Similar Delta Story Was Being Told In 2021 In a July 3, 2021 discussion on Airline Pilot Central, a moderator responded to a comment about how hard it was to get fired at Delta: Like answering your cell phone during taxi. On OE. In a follow-up, he mentioned he’d heard the story from a line check pilot. That version included the employee defending his need to stay connected during a subsequent meeting with management. By July 2025, another forum version had the Delta pilot answering because FedEx was calling about a job. Other posters mocked how often this same kind of story gets told about different airlines. And in an older Reddit discussion of pilot firings, one commenter said they’d heard a first officer using Tinder while taxiing during training story at all four airlines where they’d worked. The comments at Live and Let’s Fly reflect a split between calling it longstanding airline folklore versus supporting strict enforcement of the phone prohibition. I had much the same reaction to September’s claim that 120 pilots had been grounded for using inflight Wi-Fi. There’s a real rule against personal device use, but the particular claims weren’t well-supported. The First Officer Has Work To Do During Taxi Even when the captain has control of he aircraft, the first officer needs to monitor the aircraft’s position, clearances and other traffic. Taxiing through Atlanta isn’t downtime before the flight starts. The sterile cockpit rule covers taxi. Federal regulations prohibit distracting, nonessential activities during critical phases of flight. Those include taxi, takeoff and landing, as well as other operations below 10,000 feet except cruise. Personal phone use isn’t permissible at cruise Wireless devices and laptops are restricted at a flight crewmember’s duty station throughout flight time. (Approved electronic charts and manuals are different. It’s the device’s use, rather than who owns it, that controls. ) I’ve written that pilots should be allowed to be human, rather than expected to behave like robots throughout a long flight. That doesn’t mean taking a personal call while moving a passenger jet through an airport. Phone Distraction Has Caused Real Problems I covered a Jetstar phone-distraction incident involving a Darwin–Singapore flight where the crew hadn’t lowered the landing gear when a warning sounded at 720 feet. Their go-around began at 392 feet. The Australian investigation found that incoming message alerts sounded, the first officer saw the captain occupied with his phone, and the captain said he was unlocking it and turning it off. Jetstar added a reminder to switch phones off to its takeoff checklist and moved its landing checklist completion requirement from 500 feet to 1,000 feet, and incorporated the incident into pilot training.     • Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, an American who was reportedly yelling at staff at a hotel in Thailand ended up picking a fight with the wrong guest, and it ended up costing him his life. This is both tragic and insanely irresponsible on both sides… I just don’t get what people are thinking sometimes….

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    According to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

    Industry observers note that the confrontation escalated, and turned into a physical struggle, during which the Italian man placed the American man in a chokehold, until he lost consciousness. Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    Recent findings suggest that the Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

    I feel horribly for the family of the person who lost his life. I would have to imagine that odds are high that there were likely some substances involved here, and that this all happened after a major Saturday night out. After all, most people aren’t looking to get into a massive fight while getting their first cup of coffee in the morning (or maybe it’s just me?).

    Sources indicate that but my gosh, the “victim” here sounds like he was acting absolutely horribly, arguing with hotel staff, and then picking a fight with a random person. At the same time, that also doesn’t justify the response of getting into a conflict that leads to a fatality.

    I absolutely love Thailand — the people are so friendly, the food is amazing, and the country also offers such diversity in terms of landscape, whether you want a city, a jungle, or a beach. However, there’s also no denying that the country (and particularly Bangkok) attracts a large percentage of tourists who are looking for debauchery.

    Recent findings suggest that none of this has anything to do with a conflict that gets to the point of costing someone their life, but I can’t help but mention that when I review hotels, I tend to take a lot of pictures in lobbies around 4-5AM, when it’s the emptiest (since I’m a morning person anyway). Virtually everywhere else in the world, there’s not a single soul awake in public. Bangkok is probably the one exception, where you see a countless number of people moving through lobbies, elevators, etc., engaged in various forms of “business.”.

    Recent findings suggest that an American man lost his life in Bangkok early on Sunday morning, after picking a fight with the wrong person. The 46-year-old was reportedly shouting at hotel staff, and then attacked a 39-year-old Italian guest getting into the elevator unprovoked. That Italian man was reportedly an MMA fighter, who put him in a chokehold, to the point that the American lost his life. While the man claims he was acting in self defense, he now potentially faces manslaughter charges.

    It’s really sad how people act sometimes. We only have one life to live, and how unfortunate to cut your life short so unnecessarily.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images).

    That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

    “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

    Recent findings suggest that trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he released a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

    It has been revealed that “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

    They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

    Recent findings suggest that his interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

    It has been revealed that both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

    Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

    Recent findings suggest that “I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump mentioned as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

    “You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”.

    Trump, who was convicted by a Upcoming York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

    In a recent development, “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

    According to recent reports, other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

    And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

    Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of challenges, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

    “This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer noted.

    Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”.

    Nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He stated it was “important” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”.

    “The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”.

    Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers said they doubted very much would come from it.

    In a recent development, “I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

    “I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”.

    It has been revealed that sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

    “Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal said Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”.

    On spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

    “You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”.

    Industry observers note that john M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.

    #76822. What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1292 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane.
    • The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume.
    • Recent findings suggest that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane. So, what are the tallest and highest hotels in the world? I want to talk about that in this post, and also discuss why the answer isn’t that straightforward.

    The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume. And even once we do define it, there’s the question of the extent to which the answer is actually useful. First let’s cover the distinction between the tallest hotel and the highest hotel.

    Recent findings suggest that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel. Most commonly, I see people suggest that this would include situations where at least 80% of the building is the hotel.

    This is different than the highest hotel, which would be the hotel that is highest above the ground, even if it only takes up a small percentage of a mixed-use building, where there might be apartments, residences, etc.

    In other words, a 50-story building that consists exclusively of a hotel would fall into the former category, while a 110-story building where the top 10 floors are a hotel would fall into the latter category.

    With that out of the way, let’s talk about the properties that are remarkable in these categories….

    Recent findings suggest that first, let’s cover some of the world’s tallest hotels. We’ll define this as hotels where at least 80% of the building consists of the hotel facility.

    Let me of course mention one downside of very tall standalone hotels — you could end up being on a very low floor. After all, if a high-rise consists exclusively (or almost exclusively) of hotel facilities, some people will end up on very low floors. The other downside, of course, is that these hotels are necessarily huge. If you prefer boutique hotels, you won’t find any on this list.

    Presently, the tallest hotel in the world is Ciel Tower Dubai. The 1,042-room hotel opened in 2024, rises to a height of 1,227 feet (374 meters), and has 82 floors.

    To go over the list of the top five tallest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, it’s interesting (but perhaps not surprising) that all four of the world’s tallest hotels are in Dubai.

    The Conrad Shanghai, meanwhile, is located in the Shimao International Plaza, and this is the perfect example of how it’s tough to define what is technically the tallest. While the building it’s in rises to such a high height, roughly 25% of that height is the spire. So technically it’s a very tall building, but the usable space isn’t as high as you’d assume.

    If you ask me, the world’s highest hotels are much more interesting than the world’s tallest hotels. That’s because the world’s highest hotels typically take up the top floors of some gravity-defying skyscrapers, and therefore, they can also be boutique properties.

    When defining the world’s tallest hotels, there are some general challenges:.

    Because of the above, there are some minor disagreements as to which hotel wins the title, but I’ll share my take (while acknowledging that I don’t have the ability to scale buildings with a measuring tape).

    Currently, the highest hotel is the Rosewood Guangzhou. The 251-room hotel opened in 2019, and it’s located at the top of the CTF Finance Centre Guangzhou, which reaches a height of 1,739 feet (530 meters).

    To go over the list of the top five highest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, those last two properties are kind of hard to judge, and particularly J Hotel Shanghai is tricky, given that the property is split between different parts of the building.

    As the inverse of the above, I should mention that the Armani Hotel Dubai is located within the Burj Khalifa, which is the world’s tallest building. However, it’s located at the very bottom of the building, so that’s hardly that useful, for these purposes, since the hotel only goes as high as 39 floors.

    It has been revealed that lastly, in the interest of being thorough, if we’re going to define a hotel as being “highest” based on the altitude above sea level, then we’d of course end up with a completely different list. Hotel Tayka del Desierto is located near the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia. It’s at an altitude of 14,800 feet (4,500 meters), so it’s generally considered to be the highest up hotel in the world.

    I suppose depending on how we want to define “hotel,” there would probably be some simple guest houses at Everest Base Camp that go even higher, but I don’t think that’s within the spirit of what I’m trying to cover here.

    Industry observers note that if you ask me, it’s always fun to stay in a hotel room that’s really high up. There’s an important distinction between the tallest hotels and the highest hotels, though sometimes, the exact rankings are a bit blurred.

    In a recent development, while I’ve long been interested in this, I enjoyed researching this a bit more closely, and actually having a (sort of) definitive list. Ciel Tower Dubai is the world’s tallest hotel, while the Rosewood Guangzhou is the world’s highest hotel (unless you want to consider the 120th floor of the J Hotel Shanghai separately from the rest of the property).

    Have you stayed at any of the world’s tallest or highest hotels? Does it even hold any appeal to you?

    Having to take multiple elevators to get to the room is just not appealing to me. I”m happier in regular height hotel.

    I used to request high floors specifically, but funnily over the years, it's something I don't really care about too much anymore. The main advantage of high floors in big cities to me is that it's quieter, with less road noise. However, I generally dislike sky lobbies, especially if I have to take multiple elevators to get to my room. In some cities, it can be nice for the views, but often it's more of an inconvenience to me. Plus, it just feels more personal and (yes) "grounded" to be in a lowrise that's not part of some megacomplex. It's something I've come to appreciate more over the years.

    Industry observers note that I only care about height in the context of what kind of view it gives me. So, first I would care about far AGL (Above GROUND level, not sea level) the highest room is (assuming I can get a room on that top floor). Then I would care about how tall the surrounding buildings are and how much they block my view.

    What’s with these high hotels in the Middle East and Far East? Hmmmm!

    In a recent development, yeah, nah... The 50th floor is quite high enough for me. We have friends who live in an NYC megatall, and I wouldn't care to be perched so high up. It's unsettling.

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A Hermès carry on bag with two horse heads on the front is listed for $10,450 used, and travelers on Reddit are imagining the argument with a gate agent who wants to check it.
    • I’ve been using my Rimowa Salsa Deluxe for about a decade.
    • Recent findings suggest that here’s the Hermès Toile & Clemence R.M.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A Hermès carry on bag with two horse heads on the front is listed for $10,450 used, and travelers on Reddit are imagining the argument with a gate agent who wants to check it. I like good luggage. I’ve been using my Rimowa Salsa Deluxe for about a decade. But I don’t understand spending $10,000 on a carry on if it means worrying more about what happens to the bag than to everything inside it. Here’s the Hermès Toile & Clemence R.M.S. Cabine 55. The asking price was $11,000, reduced 5%. Hermès presently lists its Quadrige horse print cabin suitcase for $13,400 latest. Imagine the fight with the Gate Agent over checking this! What You’re Getting For The Money Reactions in the Delta thread range from hating the design to insisting that anyone with $10,000 luggage must fly private, which doesn’t make sense. They probably have no money left for even Comfort+. And there are happy owners. In a discussion among Hermès enthusiasts, one owner praises the construction and smooth wheels, while acknowledging they fly private most of the time (heh). Others worry about weight, wear and having to check it. PurseBop’s detailed owner review loves how it rolls and the ability to customize details. But the review also finds less packing space than in a Louis Vuitton Horizon because of where the telescopic handle sits. That handle arrangement also makes balancing a large tote on top less convenient. People should buy what they want. Part of being human is valuing aesthetics. A beautiful object can make someone happy every time they use it, and that has value. This particular design doesn’t do much for me, but other people don’t need to share my taste. Why I’ll Pay More For Good Luggage I used to buy whatever inexpensive bag I could find. As I traveled more, I became willing to pay for something that rolled easily, balanced properly, held what I needed and fit comfortably in the overhead bin. I wrote about that tradeoff back in 2015. A few hundred dollars spread across years of frequent travel can be a small cost per trip. Better wheels are nice every time you walk through an airport. A handle or zipper that doesn’t break saves you a hassle at exactly the moment you don’t have time for one. I still like my decade-old Rimowa Salsa Deluxe. I find Tumi overpriced for what it is, prefer Briggs & Riley for quality, and think Delsey Helium is decent at the value end. My experience with Rimowa customer service has been atrocious. When part of my handle broke, I got disconnected calls, unanswered emails and a runaround between their repair teams. By the time I reached the right people, they told me my warranty had expired in the year and a half during Covid since I’d first contacted them. First Class Doesn’t Guarantee Your Bag Stays With You Some Reddit commenters figure the owner would board early or fly first class, so gate checking wouldn’t be an issue. It doesn’t change the size of the bins on a small aircraft or help when a late connection puts you among the last passengers to board. Hermès lists its current Quadrige cabin suitcase at 22.4 inches tall. A fairly standard published limit is 22 inches, including wheels and handles. I hate gate checking bags. I don’t want my belongings lost or delayed, and I don’t want to waste time at baggage claim. When a bag comes back at the aircraft door, there’s still the wait and the extra handling. I’ve made this argument before about Louis Vuitton luggage. A bag’s job is to make its contents easy to transport and protect them along the way. If the bag itself becomes something you have to protect from ordinary travel, you’re missing the point. In 2023 I covered a traveler upset about scuffs on a Louis Vuitton carry on after Delta required it to be checked. That same year, a woman made her boyfriend give up his shirt to wrap around her $200 suitcase. This particular bag is apparently in “Excellent” condition, with “minor scratches at hardware.” For $10,450, at least somebody else has already taken care of the breaking it in.     American AAdvantage Business Program: How To Earn Bonus Loyalty Points & Miles

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1462 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that american Airlines offers a small business rewards program, known as the AAdvantage Business program.
    • Industry observers note that best of all, eligibility for the program is surprisingly simple, assuming you have the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more).
    • In a recent development, in this post, I’d like to take a look at all of the details of the AAdvantage Business program, as many people find it to be quite complicated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that american Airlines offers a small business rewards program, known as the AAdvantage Business program. This is a great way to earn extra rewards for your travel on American, including qualifying for bonus Loyalty Points and miles.

    Industry observers note that best of all, eligibility for the program is surprisingly simple, assuming you have the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more). There’s often even a bonus for latest AAdvantage Business members, making it even more rewarding.

    In a recent development, in this post, I’d like to take a look at all of the details of the AAdvantage Business program, as many people find it to be quite complicated. Note that AAdvantage Business was released in 2023, replacing the previous American Business Extra program, which no longer exists.

    AAdvantage Business is the name of American Airlines’ business rewards program. This allows you to earn extra rewards in a business account, in addition to the rewards you can earn through your own AAdvantage account. Best of all, you have quite a bit of flexibility in terms of distributing the rewards. Let’s go over the details of how this works.

    The AAdvantage Business program has a pretty straightforward rewards structure, as it rewards members with both Loyalty Points and AAdvantage miles. With the AAdvantage Business program, you earn the following rewards, which will post within 72 hours of an eligible flight:.

    Let me emphasize that business travelers only earn Loyalty Points through AAdvantage Business when the business is currently eligible to transfer miles, and that requires either having the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, or having at least five unique travelers who have credited flights to the AAdvantage Business account, totaling at least $5,000 in flight revenue, over the course of a year (the credit card method is obviously easier).

    Just to clarify a few additional points about AAdvantage Business rewards:.

    These rewards are all in addition to the standard rewards that AAdvantage members receive:.

    Just to be crystal clear, an Executive Platinum member ordinarily earns 11 Loyalty Points per dollar spent on airfare, while if enrolled in the AAdvantage Business program, they’d earn 12 Loyalty Points per dollar spent. There’s no reason to leave those bonus rewards on the table!

    According to recent reports, in order to be eligible to participate in the AAdvantage Business program, you need to have a business in the United States or Canada with a Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Business Number. Even small businesses are eligible for this program.

    Recent findings suggest that the exceptions are that travel agencies, consolidators, wholesalers, and other sellers of travel, aren’t eligible to participate in AAdvantage Business. On top of that, AAdvantage Business technically can’t be used for leisure travel.

    Recent findings suggest that you accrue rewards in the AAdvantage Business program without any minimums, and then you can transfer the rewards to individual members, so that they can then redeem them out of their own accounts. In order to transfer the miles in the AAdvantage Business account to an individual AAdvantage account, you need to meet one of two requirements:.

    Sources indicate that the AAdvantage Business program creates a huge incentive to get the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. That’s because just having the card allows many people to unlock the value of the AAdvantage Business program — there’s no need to actually use the card for your spending, but just having it is all that’s needed to redeem AAdvantage Business program rewards with no minimum on the number of travelers or revenue.

    There are several potentially useful perks to this card, and on top of that, the card is offering a great welcome bonus, which is the reason that I applied for the card (and got approved), as that’s a nice incentive, beyond the value of access to the AAdvantage Business program.

    It’s worth understanding how closely this card is actually integrated into the AAdvantage Business program:.

    Sources indicate that for American frequent flyers with a small business, this creates a strong incentive to get the card. The card has a reasonable annual fee that’s waived the first year, and just having the card will allow many people to earn a sizable number of bonus miles.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re curious about how the AAdvantage Business program works in practice, let me share some screenshots, for those who are more visual. Once you have an AAdvantage Business account, you’ll automatically become the travel manager for the account, and that means you can invite others to join your account (these should be people who work for your organization, but there’s no verification process, as far as I know).

    I should also mention that you can designate others to be travel managers as well, so that they can also invite others, transfer miles to people, etc. Travel managers must also be AAdvantage members who are adults and are residents of the United States or Canada.

    To go through the process of inviting others to join your account, you’ll want to click “Invite people,” and then once they accept your invitation, they’ll show up on your account.

    If someone’s AAdvantage account is linked to an AAdvantage Business program account, you’ll see that when you go to make a booking on aa.com, you’ll be asked for your “Travel type,” and can select “Business” or “Personal.” If you select “Business,” you’ll see that the manufacturer name populates, and you can select the name of the traveler.

    Recent findings suggest that note that AAdvantage Business bookings are limited to one passenger, so if you have multiple people traveling, you’ll need to book as separate reservations. Also, to state the obvious, AAdvantage award tickets don’t qualify.

    In a recent development, while the Loyalty Points from flights will post directly to the AAdvantage account of the member, the redeemable miles will post to the AAdvantage Business program account (the same is true for miles earned on the Citi AAdvantage Business Card). If you want to redeem miles, the only option is to transfer them to individual members, as you can’t redeem the miles directly out of the AAdvantage Business account.

    If you’re eligible to transfer those miles, you’ll see the mileage balance listed, plus a “Transfer miles” button. There’s also a dashboard that shows your eligible number of travelers and eligible spending. However, as you can see above, I’ve met the transfer conditions even though I haven’t met the required threshold, since I have the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

    Recent findings suggest that the process of transferring miles is super easy. You’ll just enter how many miles you want to transfer, and who you want to transfer them to, and then they should post to the AAdvantage account instantly.

    My general take on the AAdvantage Business program is as follows:.

    The program basically offers an incremental 1.5% return on your American spending, since you earn one extra AAdvantage mile per dollar spent, and based on my miles & points valuations, those are worth 1.5 cents each. On top of that, the program offers an incremental Loyalty Point per dollar spent — that will have no value to some, while it will have significant value to others, depending on the extent to which you’re pursuing status in the coming year.

    It is interesting the extent to which American has basically given up on corporate travel. American’s priority is getting people to book direct and keeping distribution costs as low as possible. So this program is intended as the major incentive for most small businesses.

    American Airlines offers the AAdvantage Business program. With this program, the business earns one AAdvantage mile per dollar spent on eligible airfare, while the individual traveler earns one Loyalty Point per dollar spent. In order to participate and be able to redeem miles, you need a business with at least five registered employees who have each taken at least one eligible flight, along with $5,000 in annual spending, or you need to have the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

    What do you make of the AAdvantage Business program?

    Membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

    Industry News: The House has a latest lame-duck challenge: Attendance

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S.
    • Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.
    • Sources indicate that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, said attendance is 'a great frustration.' (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.

    Sources indicate that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break. This, a day after House GOP leadership pulled a procedural rule vote when it was clear the vote might fall short because of GOP no-demonstrates – and then canceled a planned Friday voting session.

    The House has just 12 scheduled voting days left in the 119th Congress. And leaders who have at times struggled to ensure sufficient support for their agenda from the narrow majority now say they will work to make sure cases of senioritis don’t compound the problem, as both returning and nonreturning members have been part of the problem.

    "Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Thursday. “We'll be addressing that with members.".

    “We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can't do that unless people are present at work, so that's our challenge,” Johnson continued.

    Of 13 roll call votes in the House since the midterms, all but one has had a double-digit number of no-shows; for five of the 13, more than 30 members did not vote. The average number of members not voting has more than doubled since the midterm elections, compared to the final 13 roll call votes beforehand.

    It has been revealed that johnson has just a few more weeks before he steps out of the spotlight and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, takes over the GOP conference as minority leader. But his members are still counting on him to get them back to Washington.

    It has been revealed that “I think there's going to be some serious conversations over the phone, behind the scenes over the weekend,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, said. “We all took an oath of office. We have a sworn duty to be here. We're still being paid to be here, and you have to show up and do the job.”.

    And it's not just leadership that's frustrated with their missing colleagues this week.

    “There is, no question,” Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., who narrowly won reelection, responded when asked whether there was frustration in the caucus over members' absences.

    “I don't know what you do with people that don't understand the concept of duty,” Harrigan stated. “I mean, look, you signed up for a two-year term. You execute your two-year term, no matter what happens along the way politically. You have an obligation both to your constituency and to your country to be here, so the fact that they're not self-motivated to be here, I don't think that there's really much that you can do.”.

    According to recent reports, attendance has also been a bipartisan problem. A group of House Democrats, including members of leadership, faced harsh criticism from party activists for not returning to the chamber in time for a vote related to a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

    While Republican leadership grapples with the fallout from the party’s election losses earlier this month, lawmakers still face a slew of legislative items as Congress looks ahead to the holidays and a government shutdown looms.

    Many Republicans want to see a party-line defense spending bill cross the finish line, while the NDAA remains in treacherous territory and Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has been dark for months.

    However, the frustration does not lie solely with absent House members.

    “The Senate needs to do their job,” Rep. John McGuire, R-Va., mentioned. “I know we had a hard time in the midterms. History doesn't favor the party in the president's office, but we passed the Save America Act five times here. It goes over there, nothing. We've got a farm bill, nothing. We got an NDAA. We got so many things.”.

    #76816. Tech Report: Citi AAdvantage Globe Card Review—I Applied For The Bonus, But The Flight Streak Perk Is Why I Like It

    Tech Report: Citi AAdvantage Globe Card Review—I Applied For The Bonus, But The Flight Streak Perk Is Why I Like It

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 60 min read (12036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~60 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • Industry observers note that I applied for the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] when it rolled out because it was a new card I wanted to try up close and because it carried an initial bonus I hadn’t had yet.
    • Sources indicate that the reason I like having a Globe beyond the initial bonus is its Flight Streak benefit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    Industry observers note that I applied for the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] when it rolled out because it was a new card I wanted to try up close and because it carried an initial bonus I hadn’t had yet. I wound up with two Globe cards, though: the one I applied for, and a second when my Barclays AAdvantage Aviator Silver card became a Globe.

    Sources indicate that the reason I like having a Globe beyond the initial bonus is its Flight Streak benefit. You can earn up to 15,000 additional Loyalty Points each year for American Airlines flights, without putting spending on the card. I already have the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] and Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] cards for different reasons. Business is the best one for spending towards status, while Executive gives me lounge access and more bonus Loyalty Points. But Globe adds something neither of those provides.

    At $350 a year, Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is worth considering both as your main American Airlines benefits card and as an addition to the cards you already have. But you need to value the benefits and having two Globes doesn’t double the Flight Streak bonus.

    The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card awards 5,000 Loyalty Points for every four qualifying American Airlines flight segments, up to three times per status qualification year. Qualifying Segments Flown Total Flight Streak Loyalty Points 4 5,000 8 10,000 12 15,000 These are segments, so a roundtrip with a connection each way is four flights. Three of those trips can generate the full bonus. Six nonstop roundtrips would do it, too. You don’t have to buy the tickets with your Globe card. You can use another card for its rewards or protections, or fly on a ticket your employer purchases, and still earn the bonus on your qualifying travel. The qualification year runs March 1 through the last day of February. Flights must be taken after you become a primary Globe cardmember. Qualifying flights are marketed or operated by American Airlines or American Eagle and ordinarily must earn AAdvantage miles. The terms expressly include American’s basic economy segments. Award flights don’t count. The benefit belongs to the primary cardmember. Adding authorized users doesn’t give each person their own Flight Streak bonus. Citi allows 8–10 weeks after qualifying flight segments post for the additional Loyalty Points to appear. (In practice it happens promptly.) These are points toward status, not another 15,000 miles you can spend on awards. For someone already flying American regularly, this can reduce how much additional spending or other earning they need to do to reach their next status level. There’s no requirement to divert $20,000 or $50,000 of purchases from a more rewarding card. I view the card as an inexpensive way to purchase Loyalty Points which are valuable both for earning status and for additional milestone rewards. Globe And Executive Work Together—Two Globes Don’t Double The Bonus When I analyzed Globe at launch, my criticism was that Citi wasn’t giving customers much reason to keep spending on it. From the customer’s perspective, though, that’s potentially a good thing. I earn the flight bonus while putting spend wherever it makes the most sense. The Executive card by contrast includes 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points at each of 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points earned in a qualification year. Globe’s Flight Streak bonus can stack with that. Someone meeting all the requirements can earn up to 55,000 bonus Loyalty Points from the two products combined. The final Executive bonus requires reaching 240,000 Loyalty Points, so that maximum isn’t a shortcut to earning Executive Platinum from scratch. My second Citi AAdvantage Globe Card came from the April 2026 Barclays conversion. I initially wondered whether two accounts would generate two sets of flight bonuses. American subsequently confirmed to me that they wouldn’t. The Initial Bonus And Annual Fee The current offer for the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is 60,000 AAdvantage miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first three months. The annual fee is $350, isn’t waived the first year, and there’s no additional charge for authorized users. There are no foreign transaction fees. The bonus restriction is specific to the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card: you can’t have received a latest account bonus on Globe within the past 48 months, and there’s also a restriction involving another Citi account with a recent bonus that you converted into Globe. Simply having the Executive or Business card doesn’t disqualify you. What You Earn When You Spend The card’s earning categories are: Eligible Purchases AAdvantage Miles Per Dollar Loyalty Points Per Dollar AAdvantage Hotels bookings 6 1 American Airlines purchases 3 1 Restaurants, including takeout and delivery 2 1 Eligible transit, including taxis, rideshares and public transit 2 1 Other purchases 1 1 Bonus categories increase redeemable miles, not Loyalty Points. A $500 eligible American Airlines purchase earns 1,500 miles and 500 Loyalty Points from the card, in addition to whatever the passenger earns for flying. The 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are separate from the miles and Loyalty Points awarded for the hotel reservation itself. (Reserve Now, Pay Later bookings don’t qualify for the card’s 6-mile earning rate.) For my own spending, Executive already offers 4 miles per dollar on eligible American purchases (and at 4 points per dollar, I actually prefer my Chase Sapphire Reserve® [See rates and fees]) and 12 on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings. Globe’s Splurge Credit can give me a reason to charge a particular hotel purchase to it, but the regular earning rate doesn’t. For everyday purchases, one American mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar can make sense when you’re trying to reach a status threshold. Otherwise, there are better returns available. Holding Globe doesn’t obligate you to make it your everyday spending card. It’s a good card to have, not a daily spend driver outside of the quest for status. Four Admirals Club Passes Each Calendar Year Globe comes with four digital Admirals Club passes each calendar year. Each is valid for 24 hours after activation, including visits to multiple Admirals Clubs during that period. The access rules make these especially useful for an occasional traveler with children: Each adult needs a pass. Each adult using a pass can bring up to three children under 18. The primary cardmember must be present, including when using passes for adult companions. You need a same-day eligible American Airlines or oneworld boarding pass. Unused passes expire at the end of the calendar year. A couple traveling with two young children would use two passes for a travel day, rather than four. But you can’t give the passes to relatives traveling without you, and these aren’t Flagship Lounge passes or a full membership with partner lounge privileges. In my experience, the usual capacity restrictions on purchased one-day passes don’t apply to Globe passes. And just because you see a sign saying day passes aren’t being accepted doesn’t mean they aren’t being accepted – sometimes they just don’t take away the sign. American sells ordinary day passes for $79. That doesn’t make four Globe passes worth $316 to everyone. I already have Admirals Club membership through Executive, so I don’t assign these passes additional value for my own access. The Companion Certificate Doesn’t Require Annual Spending After renewing the card, starting in your second cardmembership year, you receive a certificate for one companion to travel on an eligible domestic roundtrip for $99 plus taxes and fees when you buy a qualifying Main Cabin roundtrip. However, this isn’t a certificate for any flight you want. It has fare inventory restrictions and restricted dates. You book through American Airlines Meeting Services, and travel generally must be within the contiguous 48 states on American or American Eagle. Residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have exceptions allowing qualifying trips from home to the lower 48. It doesn’t cover basic economy or partner flights. The primary cardmember must travel. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary month, and Citi allows 8–10 weeks for the certificate to become available. The certificate is valid for 12 months from issuance, with booking and travel completed by its expiration. I’ve gotten good savings from Barclays companion certificates, so I don’t dismiss these. If the eligible companion ticket would otherwise cost $500, replacing that with $99 plus taxes can cover much of the annual fee. The Credits Are Worth What They Save You Citi advertises more than $750 in value. I wouldn’t start with that number, but several benefits overlap with what I already have, and others require purchases I wouldn’t otherwise make. Up to $100 annual Splurge Credit. Choose up to two eligible merchants at a time from AAdvantage Hotels, 1stDibs, Future Personal Training and Live Nation. Activate your selection at Citi’s Splurge Credit page before purchasing. This is $100 total (not $100 per merchant). Eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are likely the most practical use for many readers. Up to $100 in annual inflight credits. Use the card for eligible purchases on domestic American Airlines or American Eagle flights. Food, drinks and eligible Wi-Fi purchases can qualify. This is less valuable when drinks are already included in your seat or status benefits, or when your flight has free Wi-Fi. Up to $240 annually with Turo. This is up to $30 per completed trip, so it takes eight trips to get the full amount. Link the card at Turo’s Globe page and pay with it directly; digital wallet payments don’t qualify. I wouldn’t assign this much value unless I were already using Turo regularly. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but I have plenty of other cards offering this reimbursement. My original reaction to the Splurge Credit was that it wasn’t worth much to me. I already have plenty of hotel credits. And an AAdvantage Hotels booking generally means giving up the hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits you’d receive by booking directly with a chain. I like the inflight credit myself now that American offers more food for purchase on more flights – I get one item free as an Executive Platinum member but I can buy sandwiches and snacks for my family. The calendar-year benefits also improve the first year. Open a card in November, and you can use available credits and passes before year-end and receive fresh allotments in January, before the next annual fee. Flight Streak resets in March. The companion certificate starts after renewal. Bags, Boarding And Other Benefits Of The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card The card provides a first checked bag free on qualifying domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Group 5 boarding also covers up to eight companions. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with Globe. Those can be valuable for someone without status, particularly a family traveling together. They add little for me because my existing status already provides better benefits. Your AAdvantage miles also don’t expire while you’re the primary holder of an eligible AAdvantage credit card. There’s also a 10% discount on eligible non-flight components of American Airlines Vacations packages booked through the designated Citi booking page. The travel and purchase protections include trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage, rental car coverage, extended warranty and purchase protection. Rental coverage is secondary in your country of residence. Citi Entertainment and Mastercard’s World Legend benefits add access to selected ticketing, dining and other experiences. I’ll Pay $350 To Keep The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card If you only want a checked bag and earlier boarding, Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] is cheaper. If you want regular Admirals Club access, Executive provides a membership for its $695 annual fee. Globe earns its place with the combination of flight bonuses, occasional lounge access and a companion certificate without an annual spending requirement. There’s a case for holding Globe alongside Executive for the additional Loyalty Points. Here’s how I’d look at renewal. If you get a real $100 of savings from the Splurge Credit, there’s $250 of annual fee left to justify through the flight bonus, companion certificate and other benefits. Earning all 15,000 Flight Streak Loyalty Points at that cost works out to about 1.67 cents per point before assigning any value to the remaining benefits. An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds. For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card.
